document.title: Sweeper Codex Desktop Communication v1
document.status: verified Windows experiments plus implementation requirements; not yet a reusable adapter
document.purpose: Record how an external Python process submits to a prepared existing Codex desktop conversation, what was tested, and which integration details remain unresolved.

sources.title: Codex non-interactive mode
sources.use: Separate execution and resume interface; not proof of delivery into a running desktop owner.

sources.title: Codex app-server
sources.use: Thread discovery, resume, and turn protocol; a newly launched server is not automatically the desktop app's server.

sources.title: Dibs wake mechanisms
sources.use: Primary project report that identified codex queue and loaded-thread limitations; local Windows tests below provide installation-specific evidence.

sources.title: Dibs native app delivery
sources.use: Version-specific macOS IPC investigation; not an implemented or Windows-verified Sweeper interface.

destination-model: The user manually creates a conversation in the correct Codex project and prepares it with Context Jetpack, coding policy, history, and project-specific instructions.
Sweeper stores the ZooKeep project GUID to Codex thread UUID association. Titles are display/discovery aids; exact [SWEEPER] is the default only when unique within the owning project folder.
The UUID in codex://threads/<uuid> is the conversation's thread ID. Use that thread ID for queue targeting; do not derive a target from the active GUI view.

Codex project IDs, ZooKeep GUIDs, and conversation thread IDs are distinct identifiers. The app-server protocol can additionally distinguish thread.id from thread.sessionId; use thread.id to address the chosen conversation.
Continuing a prepared conversation preserves access to its persisted conversation context, subject to Codex's own history/compaction behavior. It is not a promise of unlimited exact recall.

verified-environment.os: Windows; Python launched the executable through subprocess.run().
verified-environment.portability: These are experiment coordinates, not application defaults. Discover/configure the executable and destinations; the hash-named desktop binary directory can change after an update.

experiments.name: Old standalone CLI resume
experiments.method: Python launched codex exec --cd <project> resume --json <thread-id> - and supplied prompt text through stdin.
experiments.observed: The CLI resolved the thread ID but failed before model execution: model metadata parsing errors, state-database migration incompatibility, and rejection of the configured gpt-6.1-sol model.
experiments.conclusion: Do not assume a globally installed CLI is compatible with current desktop session data. This is not proof of an account-wide model restriction.

experiments.name: Desktop-bundled CLI resume
experiments.method: Python launched the newer desktop executable with exec resume for the same thread.
experiments.observed: Failed with thread-store conflict: thread already has an active writer. The desktop app owned the conversation even though its last turn had completed.
experiments.conclusion: exec resume attempts to run the conversation in another process; it does not mean send input to the existing desktop owner. Do not delete locks or kill the owner as a dispatch strategy.

experiments.name: Agent-provided desktop messaging tool
experiments.method: The coordinating agent called mcp__codex_app__send_message_to_thread with threadId and prompt.
experiments.observed: [SWEEPER] created test.json and recalled the earlier guideline about mutating global containers in place. The user saw the work in the destination chat.
experiments.conclusion: Verified the prepared destination and context. This tool is supplied to the agent by the app; the test did not establish that external Python can invoke it.

experiments.name: Python queue into loaded desktop conversation
experiments.observed: Exit 0 with queue-item UUID 01a16869-55b9-78f3-abb1-e43d55b2a6e1. Without navigating to or messaging the destination through agent desktop tools, a new turn ran and created test-queue.json in about ten seconds. Completion was subsequently observed read-only.
experiments.conclusion: External Python-to-CLI-to-existing-desktop-conversation execution is demonstrated on this Windows installation.

experiments.name: Python queue after complete desktop restart
experiments.method: The user completely exited and restarted the app. Python submitted one message to the same thread without first opening it.
experiments.observed: Exit 0 with queue-item UUID 01a16887-f203-79c0-9122-909634225ce5. No output file appeared within 45 seconds. Python then called os.startfile('codex://threads/01a16837-6e0b-7f11-8768-ee1ef2c9105a'). The same queued request created test-queue-after-restart.json about 14 seconds later. No second message was submitted. The user observed the GUI switch to that conversation.
experiments.conclusion: Queue acceptance alone did not promptly start this unloaded conversation. Opening its deeplink loaded it and enabled the retained request to run. This is one measured restart case, not a guarantee about all lifecycle states.

submission-method.python: Use subprocess with a list of arguments, shell=False, explicit project cwd, bounded timeout, and captured stdout/stderr. On Windows prefer the actual .exe over an npm shell shim. Do not interpolate request text into PowerShell or cmd command strings.
submission-method.prompt: --message accepts text. Include a readable instruction plus the serialized request JSON. The queue CLI is not a JSON-RPC endpoint and the tested queue command does not consume prompt stdin.
task-brief: Include request UUID, attempt UUID, owning project GUID and root, directive, title, description, and useful context.
Ask the prepared conversation to follow its existing project instructions. For please-investigate explicitly prohibit implementation; do not submit please-hold.
Specify result reporting separately from ordinary conversation output. A queue acknowledgment alone never means the requested work succeeded.
submission-method.receipt: Persist exit status, submission time, destination UUID, queue-item UUID when available, and concise diagnostics. Capture the command's observed output but do not depend solely on unversioned English success text; verify behavior against the selected binary.
submission-method.unknown-outcomes: A timeout, crash, or missing response can occur after enqueue. Mark delivery-unknown and reconcile; do not resubmit automatically. Opening a deeplink for an already accepted item is not a second submission.
submission-method.payload-limit: Windows command-line length bounds --message. Detect oversized argument vectors before launch. Proposed large-request mode passes a short brief referencing the durable local request file and attempt ID; verify agent readability and length handling before enabling it.

loading-policy.queue-only: Enqueue and report waiting/queued when no start evidence appears. Do not navigate the user's desktop.
loading-policy.open-on-demand: After acceptance, use verified ownership/start evidence where available. If no such observer exists, a proposed initial 45-second grace period may trigger one recorded deeplink-open attempt. Lack of a receipt is not proof that the thread is unloaded; expose the possible unnecessary navigation.
loading-policy.windows-action: Python os.startfile('codex://threads/<validated-thread-uuid>') asks Windows to open the registered desktop app route. The calling process receives no execution-completion receipt from os.startfile.
loading-policy.side-effect: The deeplink may reveal/activate the local app and change the displayed conversation. Do not open it every scan. Limit to one wake attempt per submitted attempt per observed app incarnation; further unsuccessful wakes require explicit attention.
loading-policy.deferred: Reliable app-incarnation detection, nonintrusive loaded-thread discovery, and headless loading without GUI navigation require implementation investigation. Do not claim the macOS IPC report supplies a stable Windows API.

discovery-and-executable: Manual deeplink/UUID assignment is sufficient for the first engine adapter. Full UI conversation discovery is a separate capability to implement and verify.

App-server thread/list documents filtering by cwd and title search. A Python discovery adapter must prove that it sees desktop conversations with the selected executable and state location. A CLI/server's title search is not the application's ZooKeep identity registry.
Resolve the desktop-compatible executable through configuration or a tested discovery mechanism; report its path/version in status. PATH alone selected an incompatible CLI in the experiment.
Do not alter CODEX_HOME or authentication files to evade writer ownership. Custom state locations may hide the very conversation being targeted.
Launching codex app-server creates another server. Its documented thread/resume and turn/start operations do not automatically connect to the desktop app's live owner.
A future direct local IPC adapter may improve loading and result observation, but must separately verify platform, version, supported operations, acceptance receipts, and lifecycle behavior.

result-protocol-proposal.status: Proposed extension; not demonstrated by the queue experiments and not a promise that plain Codex CLI output contains execution results.
result-protocol-proposal.method: Include the engine's absolute INCOMING directory and the expected result-signal contract in the task brief. Ask the agent to emit started and final FileTalk messages using a small documented helper when available. The engine remains the sole writer of its dispatch ledger.
result-protocol-proposal.correlation: Each result carries request UUID, attempt UUID, and destination thread UUID. Reject mismatched or unknown attempts; identical repeated receipts are idempotent.
result-protocol-proposal.outcomes: started, completed, failed, or blocked; final receipts include summary, changed files, verification performed, and any attention needed. For investigation, completed means investigation complete, not implementation performed.
result-protocol-proposal.limits: An agent can stop before writing a receipt. A receipt is agent-reported evidence, not independent proof of correctness. Missing evidence remains unresolved and queryable; never infer success from elapsed time, an empty queue, or CLI exit 0.

agent-result-signal.description: Proposed payload inside a FileTalk Core message sent to the engine; timestamp remains in the Core envelope.

next-verification: Implement and test repeatable executable and conversation discovery without assuming agent-only tools are external APIs.
Repeat queue delivery when the destination is busy and verify it does not produce overlapping project edits.
Test multiple prepared projects, missing/renamed/archived destinations, and the app not running.
Test a started/final result receipt end to end, including engine restart between enqueue and completion.
Test uncertain queue outcomes and ensure recovery never silently duplicates a request.
Test large task briefs and confirm chosen file-reference fallback behavior.
